title: Now That Jensen Huang is Out, Should Investors Buy AMD Stock Instead of Nvidia Stock? | AMD vs. NVDA
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Nvidia and AMD head-to-head now that Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO, asking which is the better buy at current prices. He floats AMD chief Lisa Su as the best candidate for Nvidia's top job, while admitting poaching her is highly unlikely. On earnings growth AMD looks better, with Wall Street forecasting about 70% EPS growth a year against Nvidia's 50%, as AMD's data-centre GPUs catch up and agentic AI makes the CPU, where AMD dominates, more important in data centres. Nvidia dominates profitability: a 65% operating margin against AMD's 17.7%, and revenue per employee of $5.5 million versus AMD's $1.17 million, though he expects the margin gap to narrow as Nvidia's near-decade-high margins fade and AMD's rise from a low base. His updated DCF cuts Nvidia's fair value from $313 to $257 after the resignation, but at about $163 the stock still looks deeply undervalued, while AMD at about $533 trades at roughly three times Nvidia's valuation. Calls: NVDA BUY at ~$163, fair value $257, reiterated from 13 November; AMD HOLD at ~$533, fair value $390, reiterated from 5 November. No flips. Bull for Nvidia: a new CEO could surprise and margins stay near decade highs. Bear: post-Jensen execution and succession risk; Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday 17 November. (Auto-captions repeatedly garble 'Jensen Huang' as 'Jensen Hong/Wong' and 'Lisa Su' as 'Lisa Sue'.)
